Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: The present study sought to extend this body of research by examining the association between the Consider subscale of the ACSS (which directly measures future interest and likelihood in having cosmetic surgery, rather than attitudinal dispositions about cosmetic surgery) and body appreciation, media influence, and respondent weight status and age. Based on previous work (e.g., Cash et al., 2005; Henderson-King & Henderson-King, 2005; Sperry et al., 2009; Swami, Chamorro-Premuzic, et al., 2009), it was predicted that participants with less body appreciation, higher internalisation of media influence, a higher body mass index (BMI), and older age would report greater consideration of cosmetic surgery.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section discusses the increasing prevalence of cosmetic procedures in developed countries, particularly among young people, and explores various correlates of interest in cosmetic surgery, such as gender, age, attractiveness, media exposure, and body image. It introduces the Acceptance of Cosmetic Surgery Scale (ACSS) and its subscales. The section concludes by outlining the present study's aim to examine the association between the ACSS Consider subscale and body appreciation, media influence, respondent weight status (BMI), and age, predicting that lower body appreciation, higher media influence, higher BMI, and older age would correlate with greater consideration of cosmetic surgery. This section describes a single 'present study'.
